workflow.name: conflict-highlight
workflow.completion_check: Repeats in a row, column or box get .cell-conflict, with no answer shown

atoms.goal: Repeated digits in a row, column or box are gently highlighted.
constraints: Compare only with other cells, never with the solution

how.steps: After every change add class .cell-conflict to every cell whose digit repeats in its row, column or box, including clue-versus-entry pairs; remove it when the repeat is gone.

expected_output.text: Conflict style exists in the page

verification.text: Conflict class is used in the page

goal.statement: Build a friendly, uncluttered Sudoku game as a single web page for casual players who play quick games on their phones, for example on a commute. It offers a few difficulty levels and beginner help that does not spoil the puzzle. It needs no sign-up and shows no ads, and it should be pleasant enough that people come back.
done_when: The page shows a 9x9 Sudoku grid with 3x3 boxes clearly marked, where the player can select a cell and enter a digit from 1 to 9 using on-screen number buttons, and erase a digit they entered
The page lets the player choose between a few difficulty levels (three or more, named in plain words) before starting, and each choice starts a new puzzle of that level
Each new puzzle is made by code in the file that guarantees exactly one solution
The page has a notes (pencil mark) mode where the player can jot small candidate digits in a cell
The page has an undo button that reverses the player's last move
The page gently highlights digits that repeat in the same row, column or box, without telling the player the correct answer
The page has a hint button that points the player to a cell or area to look at and explains why in plain words, without filling in or revealing the digit
The page shows a friendly congratulations message when the puzzle is completed correctly, with a way to start a new game
The page saves the game in progress on the player's device and offers to resume it when the player returns
The page layout fits a 360px-wide phone screen with number buttons large enough to tap comfortably and no horizontal scrolling
The page has no sign-up or login form and no ads, and the whole game is in one HTML file
The page has no JavaScript errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, and every in-page link points to an existing section.
